note: all coords in main.webp px (2400x1871). plate.webp = main.webp with the three raised arms removed and the column / back brother's red cloak / blue tunic repainted behind them (arms_hole_patch.webp = the same repaint as an opaque patch to lay over main.webp at platePatch.x,y). Draw plate, then layers in list order: arm_top, arm_mid, arm_low (back to front), sleeve_low (the front brother's lavender sleeve; it stays still and hides the root of arm_low, which carries a 16-px under-lap beneath it), swords, women. swords/women are exact cut-outs over unchanged plate pixels. Arms: rotate about pivot (shoulder end); angle = painted axis direction (screen degrees, y down, negative = up-right). arm_top/arm_mid carry ~8 px under-lap copied from the arm in front, so small relative rotation opens no slit. Keep arm rotation within about ±25 deg of the painted angle: beyond that the repainted plate and the sleeve hinge start to read as cut paper.

layers.cleanNote: same box; background fringe between the guards removed and colour neutralised to steel grey. Use it when the swords are shown on their own (rope-to-sword morph, glow, moving); use swords.webp when they sit in place over the plate (exact pixels).

geometryNote: Arches: semicircles centred (cx,springY), inner = opening (intrados), outer = brick extrados; overlaid and checked on main.webp (about ±5 px). Columns from notes.md (±15 px). convergence = least-squares meeting point of the 3 arm axes + 3 blade axes; swordHub = where the 3 blade axes meet (just below the father's fist); vanishingPoint = LSQ of floor joints + side-wall courses. The painted arms do NOT meet at one point (they fan: missAtHubX = vertical miss in px at swordHub.x); angleToConvergence / angleToSwordHub are the rotations that make each arm aim exactly there (angles in screen degrees, y down, negative = up-right).
floorOrthogonalsNote: detected joints of the floor slabs (Hough on the 3200-px source); each passes within ~20 px of vanishingPoint. Draw from vanishingPoint to bottom. Floor is visible only for y > ~1480; slab joints at x≈442/1707/1985 (row y 1700-1800). Horizontal slab edges at y≈1487, 1720, 1802.

parallelPose.note: Suggested "pulled parallel" pose for the 拉平行 interaction: rotate each arm by `rotate` degrees about `center` (the middle of its painted axis), so all three share `angle` while keeping their painted heights. Rotating the two upper arms about their shoulder pivot instead would stack them on top of each other (their visible roots are only ~8 px apart).

armAxesNote: angleToConvergence / angleToSwordHub rotate an arm about its pivot to aim exactly at that point; applied to all three arms, arm_top and arm_mid end up almost on top of each other (see contact sheet), so use those angles for drawn extension lines, not as a pose.
